title: Electrical power and energy; EMF and internal resistance
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics 2 (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: EL05-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; EL08-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; EL08-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; EL05-1#t3 term and clue written for the game. assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Power
items.clue: Rate of energy transfer, which can be found from I²R.

items.label: emf
items.clue: Energy transferred to each coulomb of charge by the source.

items.label: Short circuit
items.clue: Connection with R = 0, giving a very large current that heats the cell.

items.label: Series
items.clue: Arrangement in which a kettle element and its cable carry the same current.

questions.stem: The potential difference across an ohmic resistor is increased so that the current in the resistor becomes three times as large. What is the ratio of the new power dissipated in the resistor, P₂, to the original power, P₁?
questions.explanation: The resistor is ohmic, so R is unchanged. P = I²R: tripling I multiplies P by 3² = 9.

questions.stem: A battery with an internal resistance of 0.50 Ω drives a current of 0.60 A through a lamp, and an ideal voltmeter across the battery's terminals reads 4.2 V. The lamp is then disconnected, so that only the voltmeter remains connected across the battery. What does the voltmeter now read?
questions.explanation: emf = terminal potential difference + Ir = 4.2 + 0.60 × 0.50 = 4.5 V. With no current, the voltmeter reads the emf.

questions.stem: A steady current of 0.25 A flows in a 24 Ω resistor for 2.0 minutes. How much energy is dissipated in the resistor?
questions.explanation: Power = I²R = 0.25² × 24 = 1.5 W. Energy = power × time = 1.5 W × 120 s = 180 J.

questions.stem: A battery of emf ε and internal resistance r is connected to an external resistor of resistance R. What is the potential difference across the terminals of the battery?

Two identical heating coils, each of resistance R, are connected to the same ideal battery: first in series, then in parallel. What is the total power in parallel divided by the total power in series?
questions.explanation: Series: R_eq = 2R, so P = ΔV²/2R. Parallel: R_eq = R/2, so P = 2ΔV²/R. Ratio: (2ΔV²/R) ÷ (ΔV²/2R) = 4.

questions.stem: A battery of internal resistance r is connected to an external resistor whose resistance equals r. The external resistor is then replaced by one of resistance 2r. How does the potential difference across the terminals of the battery change?

options.text: It stays equal to its first value.
It rises to 2 times its first value.
It falls to 2/3 of its first value.
It increases to 4/3 of its first value.
